source_evidence: You could buy shares of a single company, but then your financial performance will depend exclusively on how that single company’s stock performs.
question: Misconception: Holding shares in just one company is no riskier than spreading investments across different assets because both approaches involve investing in stocks. Is this correct?
answer: No. If you invest in just one company, your financial performance depends exclusively on how that company’s stock performs. Diversifying across different kinds of assets can help reduce losses if one investment loses value, though it does not eliminate investment risk.
